_comment: Candidate local models for start_litellm_proxy.sh's interactive menu, served via mlx_vlm.server (not Ollama — see LITELLM_PROXY_USAGE.md for why). Every entry here has been through verify_max_kv_size.sh with verdict SAFE before being added; do not add a model to this file without running that script first. 'display' fields are shown to the user when picking a model, in plain language they can act on without reading the underlying research docs.

_schema_notes.serving: OPTIONAL block. Absent entirely = today's default behavior unchanged: launch_mlx_server.sh serves this entry via mlx_vlm.server with no drafter attached. When present, 'backend' selects which of the two adapter code paths the launcher uses to build its argv -- 'mlx_vlm' (same mlx_vlm.server process as always, optionally with --draft-model/--draft-kind/--draft-block-size appended) or 'mlx_dspark' (a different process, `mlx-dspark serve`, with its own flag set: --drafter/--mode/etc). The launcher branches only on this enum, never on a specific model id, so adding a new drafter-backed entry never requires editing the launch script -- only fitting one of the two existing adapters. All numeric/text fields below (measured_speedup, measured_on, greedy_divergence_observed, multimodal_capable) are informational metadata surfaced to the picker and to model_advisor.py's speed estimate -- never passed as CLI args, and never used to auto-generate a shell command from this file (deliberately: letting a data file control the executed command is an injection-shaped risk, and the memory-derived flags like --max-kv-size/--kv-bits genuinely have to be computed from the live host's free memory at launch time, not frozen into this static file). Fields: backend (mlx_vlm|mlx_dspark, required); mode (mlx_dspark only -- dflash|dspark|lookup|baseline, maps to --mode); drafter (mlx_dspark only -- HF repo id, maps to --drafter); draft_model/draft_kind/draft_block_size (mlx_vlm only -- HF repo id / dflash|mtp|eagle3 / int, map to the matching mlx_vlm.server flags); drafter_size_gb (added to size_gb by model_advisor.py's memory-fit gate, since the drafter's weights are real committed memory the base entry's size_gb doesn't include); measured_speedup (a real measured multiplier on the reference hardware in measured_on, applied on top of model_advisor.py's existing chip-scaled bandwidth formula -- not a flat absolute tok/s, so it scales down sensibly on a slower Mac than the one it was measured on; still labeled as an estimate in the picker, since the underlying accept-rate/speedup ratio could shift on a very different GPU generation); multimodal_capable (whether THIS specific serving variant retains image/video input -- false for every mlx_dspark entry, since mlx-dspark's CLI has no image/video flags at all and silently drops the vision tower on load; true for mlx_vlm+draft entries, confirmed by live-testing an actual image prompt through the drafter path, not assumed from architecture docs); greedy_divergence_observed (whether live testing at temperature=0/matched seed found the drafter path producing different token-level output than the same entry's no-drafter baseline -- both frameworks document lossless/byte-identical greedy output, and live testing found real exceptions to that claim on this specific reference hardware for some model+quant combos and not others, with no clean rule found yet for which -- e.g. Gemma-4-12B stayed identical at both 4-bit and 8-bit while Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B's 4-bit quants diverged but Qwen3.5-9B's 8-bit didn't, so this is tracked per-entry rather than assumed from the framework's own claims).
_schema_notes.type: 'dense' or 'moe'. Dense models read every weight for each decoded token; MoE models read only the routed experts plus the always-on layers, so a MoE entry must also carry active_weight_gb for model_advisor.py's speed estimate (an MoE entry without it reports 'speed unknown' rather than a guess).
_schema_notes.speed_correction_factor: OPTIONAL. Overrides the global SPEED_CORRECTION_FACTOR constant in model_advisor.py's estimate_speed_tok_s for this specific model. Added because that global constant (0.87) is confirmed NOT to hold across architecture families -- Qwen measurements cluster at 0.86-0.97, but live Gemma-4 calibration measured 1.29 (gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit) and 0.75 (gemma-4-12b-it-4bit), a 4x-wider spread in opposite directions (see HARDWARE_SPEED_ESTIMATION.md §12/§17 item #2). Populated for both of those two entries (1.281/0.756) via sweep_model.py's real per-model sweep (NEXT_SESSION_HANDOFF_PREFILL_SWEEP.md) re-deriving rather than copying the historical §12 numbers -- the fresh, independently-measured values landed within ~1% of the originals (1.281 vs 1.29, 0.756 vs 0.75), a real reconfirmation on the same chip via a different test harness/prompt shape, not a rounding artifact. Leave unset until a model has its own live-measured correction factor; the global default remains the right fallback for anything not yet measured. Superseded entirely by a saved calibration file (model_advisor.py's load_calibration) once one exists for this exact model on the current chip -- this field only matters for the formula-based fallback.
_schema_notes.active_weight_gb: MoE only. GB of weights actually read per decoded token = always-on tensors + (top_k / num_experts) x expert tensors, measured from the model's safetensors headers and config.json. Dense models omit it (size_gb is used).
_schema_notes.size_gb: Real on-disk size, measured directly (du -sh on the cached HF repo), not estimated from quantization bit-width.
_schema_notes.max_context_architectural: The model's trained/architectural context ceiling, read from its own config.json (max_position_embeddings). This is NOT the same as a safe operating context on any given machine — see recommended_max_kv_size_gb_tier (pending) once real-load memory testing is done.
_schema_notes.verification: Result of verify_max_kv_size.sh — confirms mlx_vlm.server's --max-kv-size admission gate actually rejects oversized requests for this model rather than silently ignoring them (the failure mode Ollama's MLX runner has, unfixably, per LITELLM_ROUTING_PLAN.md §4.15 and upstream Ollama issue discussion). It does NOT confirm real long-context memory safety — that needs a separate near-cap-fill test (LITELLM_ROUTING_PLAN.md §4.14 methodology) not yet run for any model in this file.
_schema_notes.tool_calling: Whether OpenCode/Claude Code's tool calls (webfetch, bash, edit, etc.) actually come back as a structured, parseable tool_calls response instead of silently degrading to plain chat text. Determined by LIVE testing (real /v1/chat/completions request with a tool schema attached, temperature=0), not by static inspection of the chat template or by which mlx_vlm tool_parser gets auto-assigned — several models (the whole qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct family) get assigned a parser (json_tools) that matches their template's markers, yet still fail live because the model itself doesn't reliably emit the <tool_call> tags its own template instructs it to use. That specific failure was independently reproduced on TWO OTHER serving stacks besides mlx_vlm (vLLM — see github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder/issues/180 — and Ollama/llama.cpp, tested directly on this machine 2026-09-28), confirming it's a property of the model's own fine-tuning, not a bug in any one harness. phi-4-mini-instruct-4bit is the opposite case: Microsoft's own model card documents real function-calling support and benchmarks it on Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard, but mlx_vlm's tool_parsers registry (mlx_vlm/tool_parsers/__init__.py's _TEMPLATE_MARKERS) has no entry matching Phi's <|tool|>/<|tool_call|> token format, so mlx_vlm never even tries to parse its output — a serving-stack gap, not a model capability gap (vLLM has a dedicated --tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json for this exact model, merged via vllm-project/vllm#14886). KNOWN GAP (historical): model_advisor.py did NOT read this field, so the interactive picker would recommend a NOT_SUPPORTED model (e.g. the former qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct or phi-4-mini-instruct-4bit entries, both since removed from this catalog — see PROJECT_STATUS.md items #20-#21) for coding tasks without warning that tool use would silently no-op. Any future NOT_SUPPORTED entry added to this catalog has the same exposure until model_advisor.py is updated to read this field. Same pattern as max_context_verified_safe's documented gap above; fixing both in model_advisor.py at the same time would make sense.
_schema_notes.status: 'tested' = run through verify_max_kv_size.sh (verification block) and a live tool-calling check (tool_calling block) on this project's mlx_vlm version. 'untested' = entry generated by add_model.py from the model's published config; the picker lists it after all tested entries, marked untested, and memory fit (kv_config/size_gb) is computed the same way, but nothing has been confirmed by actually running it. An untested entry may omit verification and tool_calling.
_schema_notes.modalities: Input modalities the MODEL supports per its own config.json (text always; image if a vision_config exists; video if it declares a video token). What a given entry actually serves is narrower when serving.multimodal_capable is false (every mlx_dspark entry is text-only) -- model_advisor.py's picker column applies that rule. Audio input is not tracked.
_schema_notes.released: 'YYYY-MM' the model was released: the base model's Hugging Face repo creation date when the repo's base_model tag names one, else the repo's own creation date (the MLX conversion usually lags the real release). Filled in by add_model.py; shown in the picker and the default sort.

display.good_for: Verifying the local model stack works end to end, and instant replies to trivial one-off questions. Not a real coding assistant — too small to trust with anything you'd actually ship.
usage_examples: "Reply with exactly the word: pong" — smoke-test that opencode/Claude Code → LiteLLM → MLX is wired up correctly before loading a bigger model
"What's the syntax for a Python list comprehension?" — quick trivia lookup, not real code generation
display.known_issues: Too small for real coding work — expect frequent mistakes on anything beyond a trivial snippet. Use only to test the pipeline itself, never as a daily driver. Observed (2026-09-29, live Claude Code test via mlx_vlm.server) getting stuck in an infinite tool-call loop on a simple single-file-read task — repeatedly re-issuing tool calls without ever converging to a final answer, instead of the single clean tool_use call the earlier structural test below showed. This is a common failure mode for small models in real multi-turn agentic loops (as opposed to a single isolated tool-call request) and is why this model is scoped to sanity-checking only, not real tool-calling usage.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. Real long-context memory load not stress-tested, but model is small enough this is low risk.

tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call (name + JSON arguments) on the first attempt, despite being the smallest model in this list (0.6GB) — structural tool-call support is not a function of model size for this family.

display.good_for: The lightest multimodal (vision-capable) option in this list — fills the gap between the tiny text-only models and the 12B+ multimodal models. "E4B" is Gemma's elastic/MatFormer naming (effective ~4B capacity), not a typo for a plain 4B model.
usage_examples: "What does this error dialog screenshot say, and how do I fix it?" — lightweight vision Q&A without the memory cost of the 12B multimodal model
"Summarize this scanned receipt/document image" — small-scale multimodal tasks on a 16-24GB Mac
display.known_issues: 131K architectural ceiling — smaller than the plain 12B/26B Gemma-4 models (262K), since this elastic variant trades some capacity for its smaller footprint. As an elastic/MatFormer model, its internal cache-building path differs from the plain Gemma-4 models — verified separately rather than assumed safe by analogy.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. First elastic/MatFormer-architecture model tested — passed despite having a different cache-building path than the plain gemma-4-12b/26b models, which was worth checking rather than assuming.

display.tagline: Same E4B multimodal model, faster via Google's own MTP drafter
display.good_for: Same vision+text capability as gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit, with a real measured ~1.56x decode speedup from Google's first-party MTP speculative-decoding drafter for this model. This is the only speed-up path available for E4B — no third-party DFlash checkpoint exists for this size, only the plain entry and this one.
usage_examples: "What does this error dialog screenshot say, and how do I fix it?" — same vision Q&A as the base entry, faster
"Summarize this scanned receipt/document image" — same multimodal task, faster turnaround
display.known_issues: Requires an extra ~0.16GB drafter download (mlx-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant-bf16). Google's own docs claim byte-identical greedy output vs. no-drafter, but live testing on this project's reference hardware found real token-level divergence from the plain entry's baseline on a text completion at temperature=0/matched seed (different wording partway through, not just a formatting difference) — looks like batched-verify-vs-serial-decode floating-point rounding on this specific GPU, not a correctness bug in the drafter, but don't assume bit-for-bit reproducibility with gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit. A separate live test with an actual image input on this same pairing stayed byte-identical, but on a short/simple completion — not enough evidence to conclude divergence is text-only.

verification.notes: Same weights as gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit, so the admission-gate result carries over. The drafter path itself was live-tested for correctness (text + image, temperature=0) rather than assumed — see known_issues for the divergence found.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request directly against mlx_vlm.server with --draft-model/--draft-kind mtp attached (this exact pairing), web_search tool schema, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call, with the response's own draft_kind=mtp/draft_rounds/draft_n_accepted fields confirming the drafter was genuinely active while producing the tool call, not silently bypassed for tool-call requests.

display.tagline: Lighter version of our trusted 12B multimodal model
display.good_for: Same model as gemma-4-12b-it-8bit already in this list (proven safe), just 4-bit instead of 8-bit — meaningfully lighter (6.31GB vs 12GB) for a 16-24GB Mac that still wants vision support.
usage_examples: "What's wrong with this UI based on the screenshot?" — visual analysis, same capability as the 8-bit version
"Describe the architecture shown in this diagram" — vision+text reasoning with more memory headroom left over
display.known_issues: Same thermal/efficiency caveat as the 8-bit sibling (Gemma-4's architecture is less MLX-efficient at long context than Qwen3.5's). 4-bit quantization trades some accuracy for the smaller footprint versus the 8-bit version. IMPORTANT, live-tested 2026-10-05: on mlx_vlm, a growing multi-turn conversation (same session, appended turn) gets ZERO prompt-cache reuse on every turn -- cached_tokens:0 even though exact byte-for-byte repeat requests cache correctly (hit_rate 1.0). Root-caused directly from this model's own cached chat_template.jinja: the add_generation_prompt branch appends a 4-token empty '<|channel>thought\n<channel|>' marker before a fresh non-thinking generation, but the main per-turn loop does NOT reproduce that marker when re-serializing a completed assistant turn into history -- so the reconstructed prefix for turn N+1 diverges from what was actually prefilled for turn N starting 4 tokens before the end, and mlx_vlm's APC 'checkpoint' strategy for Gemma-4's hybrid sliding-window cache requires an exact full-prefix hash match (all-or-nothing), so it misses entirely rather than partially. This is a HuggingFace model-repo chat-template bug, not an mlx_vlm/mlx-dspark code bug -- upstream mlx-vlm PR #1960 ('Redesign APC for dense and hybrid model caches', merged 2026-08-28, included in our pinned 0.7.4) documents and fixes this EXACT bug ('appended a four-token empty thought channel ... did not reproduce it when serializing that assistant turn into history') via linked template-fix discussions on the *5-bit* HF repos (huggingface.co/mlx-community/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-5bit/discussions/2 and .../gemma-4-31b-it-5bit/discussions/2) -- NOT on this 4-bit repo or the 8-bit sibling, whose chat_template.jinja was directly inspected here and confirmed to still carry the unfixed template. The same PR's own validation of a real gemma-4-12b-it-8bit server independently reported the same symptom ('the gemma4_unified multi-turn template rewrote the previous token stream'). mlx-dspark backend (gemma-4-12b-it-4bit-dflash) hits the identical template bug but degrades more gracefully: its prefix matcher tolerates the trailing mismatch and still reuses tokens up through the divergence point (measured cached_tokens:1517/1540 vs mlx_vlm's 0/1540 on an identical growing-conversation request), so only ~1-2% of each turn's tokens are needlessly re-prefilled instead of 100%. gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit/gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit are NOT affected -- their chat_template.jinja has no such marker in the add_generation_prompt block at all (confirmed by direct diff), and their growing-conversation caching was independently verified correct (cached_tokens:1516/1536).

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds.

display.known_issues: IMPORTANT: this mode drops image/video input entirely — mlx-dspark's CLI has no image/video support at all and silently ignores the target's vision tower on load. Use the plain gemma-4-12b-it-4bit entry for anything involving an image. Requires an extra ~1.45GB drafter download (z-lab/gemma4-12B-it-DFlash). Live-tested at temperature=0/matched seed against the plain entry's baseline and found byte-identical greedy output — no divergence observed for this specific model+quant, unlike some of the other drafter-backed entries in this file. Shares the same chat_template.jinja growing-conversation cache-miss bug as the plain gemma-4-12b-it-4bit entry (see its known_issues for the full root cause), but degrades more gracefully here: live-tested 2026-10-05, mlx-dspark's prefix matcher tolerated the ~4-token trailing mismatch and still reused tokens up through the divergence point (cached_tokens:1517/1540 on a growing-turn request) instead of mlx_vlm's all-or-nothing 0/1540 miss on the identical request shape -- so only ~1-2% of each turn's tokens are needlessly re-prefilled here, not the full turn.

verification.notes: Same weights as gemma-4-12b-it-4bit, so the admission-gate result carries over for the target itself. mlx-dspark's own admission/context handling was not separately run through verify_max_kv_size.sh (that script targets mlx_vlm.server specifically) -- the drafter path's decode correctness was live-tested directly instead (temperature=0, matched seed vs. baseline), which is what known_issues reports.

display.good_for: The only way to get any decode speedup on this model while keeping image/video input — mlx-dspark (the faster drafter backend) cannot process images at all. Runs the same DFlash drafter as gemma-4-12b-it-4bit-dflash, but through mlx_vlm.server's own native --draft-model support instead of mlx-dspark, since mlx_vlm is the multimodal-capable server.

"Compare these two screenshots and describe what changed" — multimodal task where some speedup is still welcome
display.known_issues: IMPORTANT, and notably DIFFERENT from the text-only gemma-4-12b-it-4bit-dflash entry: live-tested with real image prompts at temperature=0/matched seed and found real token-level divergence from the plain entry's baseline on two of the three prompts (different but plausible wording — e.g. the same plain background described as a 'subtle horizontal pinstripe pattern' vs. a 'fine-grained noise or speckled texture' — plus a different completion length on the description prompt), even though this exact model+quant stayed byte-identical under mlx-dspark's own DFlash implementation on a text prompt. The 8-bit sibling's vlm variant (gemma-4-12b-it-8bit-dflash-vlm) diverged in its own test too — for the Gemma-4-12B family the mlx_vlm drafter path has now diverged on both quants tested while mlx-dspark stayed identical on both, the exact opposite pattern from the Qwen3.5 4-bit quant. Also measurably slower than the mlx-dspark text-only entry (~1.55x here vs. ~2.21x there), for the same reason documented on the Qwen3.5 vlm variants: mlx_vlm's native path lacks mlx-dspark's automatic per-machine draft-block-size calibration. --draft-block-size 4 kept after a manual sweep on this pairing (3 measurably worse; 4/5/6 within single-run noise of each other). Requires an extra ~1.45GB drafter download (z-lab/gemma4-12B-it-DFlash) — same file as the mlx-dspark entries above, so no extra download if you already have one of those. Also runs through mlx_vlm.server (same as the plain gemma-4-12b-it-4bit entry), so it inherits that entry's growing-conversation APC cache-miss bug too (chat_template.jinja root cause, see its known_issues) -- not independently re-tested with the drafter attached, but the underlying prefix divergence happens before the drafter is even reached.

verification.notes: Same weights and same server (mlx_vlm.server) as gemma-4-12b-it-4bit, so the admission-gate result carries over directly. The drafter path itself was live-tested for correctness with three real image prompts (temperature=0, matched seed vs. baseline) and found to diverge on two of them -- see known_issues.

IMPORTANT, live-tested 2026-10-05: on mlx_vlm, a growing multi-turn conversation (same session, appended turn) gets ZERO prompt-cache reuse on every turn -- cached_tokens:0, reproduced twice with different prefixes, even though exact byte-for-byte repeat requests cache correctly (hit_rate 1.0). This is NOT a MoE-specific bug (an earlier working hypothesis on this project that a dense-vs-MoE split explained it was tested and disproven -- the dense gemma-4-12b-it-4bit shows the identical symptom on mlx_vlm, while the dense gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit does not). Root-caused directly from this model's own cached chat_template.jinja (byte-identical to gemma-4-12b-it-4bit's): the add_generation_prompt branch appends a 4-token empty '<|channel>thought\n<channel|>' marker before a fresh non-thinking generation, but the main per-turn loop does NOT reproduce that marker when re-serializing a completed assistant turn into history, so the reconstructed prefix for turn N+1 diverges from what was actually prefilled for turn N starting 4 tokens before the end -- and mlx_vlm's APC 'checkpoint' strategy for Gemma-4's hybrid sliding-window cache requires an exact full-prefix hash match (all-or-nothing), so it misses entirely. This is a HuggingFace model-repo chat-template bug, not an mlx_vlm/mlx-dspark code bug -- upstream mlx-vlm PR #1960 ('Redesign APC for dense and hybrid model caches', merged 2026-08-28, included in our pinned 0.7.4) documents and fixes this EXACT bug via a linked template-fix discussion on the *5-bit* HF repo specifically (huggingface.co/mlx-community/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-5bit/discussions/2) -- NOT on this 4-bit repo, whose chat_template.jinja was directly inspected here and confirmed to still carry the unfixed template (identical to the 12b-it-4bit file). gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit/gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit are NOT affected -- their chat_template.jinja has no such marker in the add_generation_prompt block at all.

tool_calling.notes: finish_reason=stop, tool_calls=null, but reasoning_content correctly shows the model deciding to call the tool (e.g. 'We need to search the web. Use web_search.') -- the model knows what to do but the structured call never comes back. Root-caused, not just observed: bypassing mlx_vlm.server entirely and calling mlx_lm.generate() directly on the same model/prompt/tools produced a complete, correctly-formatted harmony tool call (`<|channel|>commentary to=functions.web_search <|constrain|>json<|message|>{"query":"..."}`) followed by the model's own <|call|> stop token -- proving the MODEL and the harmony parser are both fine. The bug is specific to mlx_vlm.server's generation loop: it stops right after the 'analysis' channel's closing <|end|> token (id 200007) and never continues into the 'commentary' channel at all, even though <|end|> is NOT one of the model's own registered eos_token_id values (generation_config.json: 200002 <|return|>, 199999 <|endoftext|>, 200012 <|call|> -- confirmed via tokenizer.decode on this exact model). Likely proximate cause: mlx_vlm/models/gpt_oss/processing_gpt_oss.py's HARMONY_RESPONSE_TEMPLATE marks the merged analysis/commentary 'reasoning_content' field as `"close": ["<|end|>"], "repeats": True`, and the server's response-template state machine (mlx_vlm/server/responses_state.py) appears to end the whole generation after the first repeat instead of continuing for the commentary-channel tool call that should follow. Not yet traced to the exact line/condition inside responses_state.py -- that would be the next step before filing an upstream issue. This means every example in this catalog that recommends gpt-oss-20b-mxfp4-q8 for agentic tool-use is currently wrong on this mlx_vlm version; OpenCode/Claude Code's actual tools (bash, edit, webfetch, etc.) would silently no-op against this model exactly like the already-documented qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct family, but for a completely different reason (server-side generation cut short, not a model formatting failure). Follow-up research (not independently verified -- see HARDWARE_SPEED_ESTIMATION.md section 21): llama.cpp has a dedicated, grammar-constrained harmony tool-call parser for gpt-oss and is reported reliable as of this research, but this project has no llama.cpp integration and did not live-test it.

display.known_issues: ❌ TOOL CALLS DO NOT PARSE on mlx-lm 0.31.3 / mlx-vlm 0.7.4: live testing showed the model emits valid Qwen3-Coder XML (<tool_call><function=get_weather><parameter=city>Tokyo</parameter></function></tool_call>), but its chat_template.jinja writes <tool_call><function= without a newline, causing mlx_lm.tokenizer_utils._infer_tool_parser (which checks for "<tool_call>\n<function=") to miss qwen3_coder and fall back to json_tools. json.loads() then fails and mlx_vlm.server leaks the raw <tool_call> XML into message.content with tool_calls=null. Additionally, the vision tower was dropped in this OptiQ conversion (text-only).

verification.notes: verify_max_kv_size.sh confirmed clean HTTP 400 admission-gate rejection at both the moderate scale (bound=256 vs a 765-token prompt) and the extreme scale matching upstream mlx_vlm PR #1995's own reproduction (bound=32 vs a 69-token prompt, max_tokens=1) -- no silent truncation/ignoring of --max-kv-size. The script's automated moderate-scale RECALL check could not run to completion for this reasoning model (its fixed 60-token completion budget is spent entirely inside a <think> block, never reaching a final answer -- finish_reason=length, not an enforcement failure: 765+60=825 tokens stayed under the 1024 bound the whole time). Recall correctness was confirmed manually instead with a short prompt and a completion budget large enough for the reasoning chain to finish (this entry: 400-token budget, 290 used, exact correct recall, finish_reason=stop) against the same --max-kv-size 1024 server. Full probe JSON for both the automated and manual checks is in mlx_verification_results.json. Also fixed, while running this: verify_max_kv_size.sh's own health check had a latent bug (unrelated to this model) where /v1/models on this project's mlx_vlm 0.7.4 lists the WHOLE on-disk HF cache rather than just the loaded model (an apparent behavior change since the script was last validated against mlx_vlm 0.7.0, per its own header comment) -- the script read data[0] assuming it was always the just-started model, which produced a false 'stale process' error for every model, not just this one. Script now matches by id + loaded:true instead of array position. Full writeup: PHASE_PLAN.md, "Research: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B added..." (2026-10-03).
